question: Which exact 3.101.043 callable preserves the 3.101.036 LVX image scale behavior used by LyraPlayer controls?
callsite_evidence: The working 3.101.036 callable is sub_C179A8C at 0x0C179A8C with prototype void(void *, int32_t, int32_t).
The 3.101.036 function is 0x14C bytes, stores the second and third AAPCS arguments together at image-object offsets +0x50/+0x54, and invalidates the old and new transformed bounds around the write.
LyraPlayer's working 3.101.036 control path passes equal x/y scale values in 1/256 units to this callable.
control_flow_evidence: Exact 3.101.043 sub_C179DB0 at 0x0C179DB0 is also 0x14C bytes and has the same seven-block control-flow graph as 3.101.036 sub_C179A8C.
The two functions preserve the same instruction sequence, object offsets, constants, argument registers, branch structure, and seven stock callsites; only relocated callee addresses differ.
At 0x0C179E3E the exact 3.101.043 function executes STRD R1, R2, [R4,#0x50], proving the same three-argument image-pointer/x-scale/y-scale ABI.
The generated exact-target callable is 0x0C179DB1 and remains restricted to the UI owner thread.
ownership_analysis: The first argument is a borrowed firmware LVX image object. The callable mutates only the object's transform fields and firmware-managed invalidation state; LyraPlayer retains no firmware-owned pointer beyond the page lifecycle.
unsafe_assumptions: Static equivalence does not replace an exact 3.101.043 touch-and-animation device gate.
Scale calls must remain on the firmware UI owner thread and receive a live LVX image object.
recommended_probe: Open LyraPlayer on exact 3.101.043, press previous/play/next repeatedly, and compare normal (192/256) and pressed (100/256) control rendering and touch dispatch with the known-working 3.101.036 build.
